subject: mathematics_1b
question_text: Find the distance between the parallel lines 3x+4y−3=0 and 6x+8y−1=0.

recall_prompt: Say how you would solve this — say what must be true of the two equations before the formula can be used.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Match the coefficients
steps.margin_note: First mark, and the step the whole question turns on. The distance formula only works when BOTH lines carry the SAME a and b, so rescale one of them first.
steps.memory_tip: The formula only works when BOTH lines carry the SAME a and b — rescale one first.
lines: We write the first line 3x + 4y − 3 = 0 as

recall.must_convey: That one line is rescaled so both lines have identical x and y coefficients.
accept: multiply the first line so both have the same coefficients
the formula needs identical a and b in both lines
rescale one equation to match the other
rendu lines lo a b same ga undali

steps.why: Using the formula on mismatched coefficients gives a number that is wrong by exactly the scale factor — this is the single commonest error in the question type.
common_mistakes: Rescaling the x and y terms but forgetting the constant.

steps.label: Apply the distance formula
steps.margin_note: Second mark. With matched coefficients, the distance is |c₁ − c₂| over √(a² + b²).
steps.memory_tip: With matched coefficients the distance is |c₁ − c₂| over √(a² + b²).

recall.must_convey: That the formula |c₁ − c₂|/√(a² + b²) gives 1/2.
accept: use mod c one minus c two over root a squared plus b squared
apply the distance between parallel lines formula
the difference of the constants over the root
c one minus c two mod, root a square plus b square tho divide
heard_as: root a squared plus b squared

steps.why: Only the constants differ once the coefficients match, so their difference measures the gap — divided by the length of the coefficient vector to convert it into a true distance.
common_mistakes: Adding the constants instead of subtracting.
Forgetting the square root in the denominator.

insider_note: The two lines must carry IDENTICAL coefficients first, so double the first to 6x + 8y − 6 = 0. Rescaling the x and y terms but leaving the constant at −3 is what makes this come out wrong.
